summary: A tense two-player card-drafting duel where one side plays the Fellowship racing to destroy the Ring and the other plays Sauron building armies and corrupting the map, with area-majority control over Middle-earth's regions deciding momentum each chapter. It plays fast and tight, with several different ways for either side to trigger a sudden-death win before the final scoring even happens.
praised: Tight, tense two-player design from experienced co-designers
Strong thematic integration of Fellowship vs Sauron asymmetry
Multiple paths to instant victory keep every turn meaningful
Quick to teach and play (30 minutes) while staying strategically dense
criticised: Inevitable comparisons to 7 Wonders Duel as derivative rather than fresh
Asymmetric factions can feel unbalanced or favor one side in early plays
Card draw/setup variance can swing a short game significantly
Sudden-death win conditions can end games abruptly before a side feels they've had their turn

interaction.kind: area control and open conflict over a shared card row and map

scoring.why: The winner is decided either by triggering one of several sudden-death conditions (quest completion, army advance, area domination) or by comparing accumulated points/board state if the chapters run their course

_name: The Lord of the Rings: Duel for Middle-earth
